subject: Post-demo pricing alignment & $/1M token benchmarking
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 14:30:00 -0500
Subject: Post-demo pricing alignment & $/1M token benchmarking

Alex — great to meet today. Quick recap from our demo and next steps on pricing so we can align on a target $/1M tokens for your procurement team.

TL;DR: FinLytics is targeting a sustainable unit cost in the low teens per 1M tokens for nearline inference (high-throughput embeddings + retrieval-augmented generation), with a phased volume ramp (month 1: ~50M tokens, steady-state: 800M–1.2B tokens/month). You asked for competitive benchmarks vs OpenAI/Anthropic and what Redwood can hit with hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments.

Call notes and assumptions:
- Workload mix: 70% embeddings (short context), 30% completion/chat (avg response length ~600 tokens).
- Expected monthly tokens: 50M -> 1.2B (6–12 month ramp).
- SLO: 95th pctl latency target 300ms for embeddings, 500ms for chat (hosted or dedicated).

Benchmarks (approximate, model + hosting dependent — shown as $ per 1M tokens):
- OpenAI (curated hosted models): $30–$110 / 1M tokens depending on model family and context length.
- Anthropic (hosted): $25–$90 / 1M tokens.
- Public cloud self-host (large model, quantized): $8–$35 / 1M tokens (infrastructure + ops).
- Redwood Hosted (managed): $18–$50 / 1M tokens (we optimize batching, caching, and model routing).
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPUs, committed volumes): $6–$20 / 1M tokens (volume + commitment-dependent).

Suggested target and reasoning:
- For a vendor you want predictable unit economics for steady-state at ~1B tokens/month, a realistic target range is $8–$15 / 1M tokens if you commit to Dedicated/reserved capacity with a 12–24 month contract.
- If you need self-hosted Private deployment (air-gapped / on-prem), economics shift toward $5–$18 / 1M tokens depending on hardware amortization and whether you want Redwood to manage the control plane.

Action items (proposed):
1) FinLytics: confirm target steady-state monthly token volume (best guess by month for next 6 months).
2) Redwood: provide an apples-to-apples pricing matrix (hosted vs dedicated vs private) with modeled unit economics for the workload mix you shared — I attached a starter matrix.
3) Procurement: indicate preferred procurement timeline and any required security attestations (SOC2, data residency).

Attachments: Redwood-pricing-matrix-2026Q1.xlsx, 1M-token-benchmark-chart.png (sent after call).

If this looks right, Alex, I’ll convert the matrix to a formal quote with two commit scenarios (12-month and 24-month) and a fallback plan for burst capacity.

Cheers,
Grace
Grace O'Connor

Grace — thanks for the summary. A couple quick clarifications for procurement:  
1) When you say $8–$15 /1M tokens for Dedicated, is that predicated on a 12-month commit at what monthly volume?  
2) We’ll need an apples-to-apples line-item showing infra, model licensing (if any), and Redwood platform fee so our finance team can compare.

Our rough ramp (internal): month 1: 50M, month 3: 200M, month 6: 700M, month 9–12: targeting 1B+.

Procurement timeline: want initial T&C and blank SOW by March 12, internal approvals by March 26. SOC2 evidence required.

If you can provide a few fixed scenarios (no commitment / 12mo / 24mo) with explicit $/1M math, we can run the TCO model.

Also, curious: how often would Redwood recommend model switching to cheaper variants and what unit-econ delta do you typically capture?

— Alex

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-demo pricing alignment & $/1M token benchmarking

Alex — great questions, answered inline and attached a filled pricing matrix (stub) for the ramp you listed.

1) Assumptions behind $8–$15 /1M tokens for Dedicated:
   - 12mo commit baseline example: steady-state 1B tokens/month -> $8–$12 /1M tokens (higher end if you require lower-latency GPUs or specific model families).
   - 24mo commit example: $6–$10 /1M tokens due to deeper discounts on reserved GPU blocks and predictable scheduling.
   - No-commit hosted pricing will be 1.8–3x higher on the same models due to spot/reservation differences.

2) Apples-to-apples line items (provided in spreadsheet):
   - Infra (GPU time + networking + storage) — expressed as $/inference-hour and converted to $/1M tokens for your mix.
   - Model execution (licensed model or open checkpoints operational cost).
   - Redwood platform fee (management, routing, caching, monitoring).
   - Optional add-ons (extended obs retention, private control plane).

Model switching and unit-econ delta:
- Typical opportunity: routing lower-latency/low-cost requests to quantized open models and routing high-accuracy requests to larger models. We’ve seen 20–60% unit-cost reductions on retrieval-heavy workloads by combining KV caching + model routing. Example: replacing a high-cost completion model for short answers with a 1-bit quantized open model for embeddings + a small chat model saved ~28% on $/1M tokens in a recent customer case.

Next steps I’ll take now:
- Convert spreadsheet into 3 quote scenarios (no-commit hosted, 12mo dedicated commit, 24mo dedicated commit) with explicit $/1M numbers for the ramp you provided.
- Attach SOC2 evidence and a short note on data residency for EU/US.

Alex — expect the matrix + preliminary quote by EOD tomorrow. If procurement needs a template SOW, I’ll loop legal.

Thanks,
Grace
